user.title: ClimateML
user.description: Add the ClimateML integration. Add zones and configure the controller via the integration page after setup.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one ClimateML instance is allowed

data_description.name: Display name — also generates the stable internal zone ID
data_description.head_entity: The climate entity for this zone — ClimateML will command it for both cooling and heating
data_description.sensor_entity: Actual room temperature sensor — the reference used to calculate offset corrections
data_description.eva_in_entity: Refrigerant temperature entering the indoor unit — logged for future ML efficiency analysis
data_description.eva_out_entity: Refrigerant temperature leaving the indoor unit — logged for future ML efficiency analysis
data_description.occupancy_entity: Presence sensor for this zone — used later to adjust behaviour when the zone is unoccupied
data_description.weekday_blocks: Cooling and heating schedule for Monday–Friday
data_description.weekend_blocks: Cooling and heating schedule for Saturday–Sunday

data_description.name: Display name — also generates the stable internal zone ID

data_description.eva_out_entity: Refrigerant temperature leaving the indoor unit — logged for future ML efficiency analysis
data_description.occupancy_entity: Presence sensor for this zone — used later to adjust behaviour when the zone is unoccupied
data_description.weekday_blocks: Cooling and heating schedule for Monday–Friday
data_description.weekend_blocks: Cooling and heating schedule for Saturday–Sunday

data_description.update_interval_minutes: How often ClimateML recalculates and commands each zone — lower is more responsive, higher sends fewer commands
data_description.setpoint_min_c: Lowest temperature ClimateML will ever command to any zone climate entity
data_description.setpoint_max_c: Highest temperature ClimateML will ever command to any zone climate entity
data_description.odu_mode_entity: Current operating mode of the outdoor unit — used to know when the system is actively conditioning
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Outside air temperature — used as a peer reading in the sensor guard anomaly check
data_description.extra_temp_entities: Non-zone indoor sensors (hallway, landing, etc.) — used as peer readings in the sensor guard
data_description.power_entity: Real-time system power draw — logged for future efficiency and COP tracking
data_description.energy_entity: Cumulative system energy use — logged for daily efficiency trends
data_description.weather_entity: Provides hourly forecasts for anticipating solar gain and outdoor conditions (future ML)
